[0] everyday_reading (E): Everyday reading: 'error' means the program will do something wrong when used, and a message points exactly at the mistake. Java rule: a compile-time error is a breach of the language rules found by javac before any execution; no .class is produced, and the reported line is where javac noticed it.
[1] misconception (M) -> CompilesMeansWorks: wrong rule: Code that compiles is code that works. Right rule: Compiling only checks the language rules; code that compiles can still have run-time and logic errors.
[2] misconception (M) -> ErrorLineIsFaultLine: wrong rule: The line number in a javac error is always the line that has the mistake. Right rule: The compiler reports where it noticed the problem, which can be after the real fault (omitting HelloWorld's second left brace gives errors on later lines).
[3] inconsistent_trace (T) -> CompilesMeansWorks: Applies the 'javac checks before running' rule unevenly: predicts output for a program that would not compile, or expects a compile error from a fault (such as division by zero) that only shows at run time. (here mixing in: "Code that compiles is code that works")
[4] misconception (M) -> CompilerSuggestionIsFix: wrong rule: Doing exactly what the compiler message suggests will fix the error. Right rule: An error message is evidence that something is wrong, but its suggested remedy may be wrong; find the actual cause.

[0] names_the_element (N): A compile-time error (syntax error) is an error in the source code, caught by javac, that prevents the program from being translated.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Compile-time errors occur when the code violates the rules of the Java language (syntax, names, types); they are caught when you compile and prevent the translation.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): javac reads the whole file, reports each error with file name, line number and message, tries to recover and continue, and prints a count; the first message is the most reliable.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Result: messages such as Bad.java:4: ';' expected ... 3 errors, and no Name.class; nothing of the program runs.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): A failed compile leaves the file system without a new Name.class (an older one, if any, is not updated) and changes no program state.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): A compile-time error is reported while javac compiles Name.java, so no new Name.class is produced.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): Each compile-time error comes with a message; reading it (first error first, line may be late) is how it is found and fixed.
[2] relation_to_neighbour (R): A compile-time error is found by javac before the program runs; a run-time error only while it runs, so code that compiles can still crash.
[3] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Purpose (of the check): catch rule violations automatically before running, so they cannot cause wrong behaviour; S&W say treat the compiler as a friend.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> CompilesMeansWorks: Fixing the first error and recompiling can remove many messages at once; a single missing brace or semicolon can cause several messages.
[1] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Each statement must end with ;. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: missing ; at the end of a statement: ';' expected
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Every { must be matched by a }. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: missing or extra brace: '{' expected, 'class' or 'interface' expected, reached end of file while parsing
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: A String literal is enclosed in a pair of double quotes. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: missing closing quote: unclosed string literal, often with confusing follow-on errors
[4] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Library static methods are called with the class name, e.g. Math.sqrt(x). Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: calling sqrt(x) without Math.: cannot find symbol
[5] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Every name must be spelled exactly, including capitalization. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: Sytem.out.prinln, Println, or a misspelled variable: cannot find symbol
[6] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: A /* comment needs its closing */. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: /* with no */ swallows the rest of the file
[7] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Expect compile-time errors for anything the compiler can check from the text alone (syntax, names, types, final); expect run-time or logic errors for faults that depend on input values or on what the program was meant to do.
[8] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: A final variable cannot be reassigned after it is initialized. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: assigning a second value to a final variable
[9] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Required keywords (class, static, void...) must be present and spelled right. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: omitting or misspelling a keyword in public class Name or the main header
